newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish treasury wants new Polifarb issue.
newsitem.headline: Polish treasury wants new Polifarb issue.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry asked the Polifarb Wroclaw paintmaker to call an extraordinary meeting to vote on a proposal of a bonus issue of between 6.375 million and 10 million shares, the company said on Monday.

Polifarb Wroclaw said in a statement the ministry also wanted shareholders to vote on changes in earlier resolutions passed on the allocation of 1996 profits and the planned merger with Polifarb Cieszyn.
The statement did not give any further details and neither the company nor ministry officials were immediately available for comment.

Any shareholder which has more than 10 percent of a company, and the ministry holds 16 percent in Polifarb Wroclaw, is entitled to request an extraordinary shareholders meeting to vote on its proposals.

The move comes apparently as a reaction to Polifarb Cieszyn shareholders' decision to change late last month the conditions of a planned merger by a capital rise, which would give Cieszyn shareholders a bigger stake in the new company.

Cieszyn shareholders approved a version of the merger giving them 53.5 percent rather than 50 percent of the new firm by increasing a planned pre-merger bonus issue for Cieszyn shareholders to 6.375 from 2.98 million shares.
Cieszyn currently has 19,125,000 shares, 2,978,820 fewer than Wroclaw and a new bonus issue was originally designed to make up for the difference.
